📌 London, IRNA — Iran’s Ambassador and Permanent Representative to International Organizations in Vienna stresses that Tehran will not submit to unrestricted inspections under continued military threats, stating that any request from the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) will be decided based on security considerations.

The full text of Reza Najafi’s speech at the Board of Governors of the IAEA on the Nuclear Program of the Islamic Republic of Iran (Vienna, 18 November 2026) is as follows:
​
I associate myself with the joint statement of China, Iran and Russia.
​
Reiterating Iran’s consistent and strong objection to derestricting the DG’s report, I inform you that our position on the report is reflected in INFCIRC/1442.
​
I wish to begin with this part of the Director General’s report: “It is more than a year since the Agency lost continuity of knowledge.”
​
It is simply a partial, inconclusive fact on Iran’s peaceful nuclear program.
​
There are more important realities that this Board cannot ignore.
​
The first fact is that Iran has engaged seriously and extensively with the Agency over years in order to address possible concerns, and in 2015, with “the Final Assessment,” all past issues were closed by this very Board.
​
In the same year, the JCPOA, concluded after years of intensive negotiations among Iran, the P5+1 and the EU and endorsed by the Security Council in resolution 2231, stands as the clearest example of that record.
​
Iran’s cooperation has gone beyond its legally binding obligations, including the limitation on uranium enrichment for a long period and the voluntary implementation of the Additional Protocol for extended periods, although Iran never ratified it.
​
16 consecutive Agency reports verified Iran’s full implementation of its JCPOA commitments.
​
On 5 March 2018, the then Director General of this Agency stated, and I quote: “The IAEA now has the world’s most robust verification regime in place in Iran.” “Our current verification capability is much stronger than it has ever been.”
​
He added, and again I quote: “We have had access to all the locations that we needed to visit. Our inspection work has doubled since 2013. IAEA inspectors now spend 3,000 calendar days per year on the ground in Iran. We have installed some 2,000 tamper-proof seals on nuclear material and equipment.”
​
These are not Iran’s claims; they are the explicit, word-for-word statements of the Director General of this very Agency, made on the record, and no one in this room can dismiss them as political.
​
By the Agency’s own figures, between 2013 and 2017 its verification activities in Iran rose by 152 percent.
​
Iran also accounted for about half of all images collected daily by the Agency’s global surveillance network.
​
Annual verification costs rose by 230 percent and inspector field days by 100 percent.
​
Such an unprecedented scope of verification was simply impossible without Iran’s complete cooperation.
​
The second fact is that this loss of continuity has a cause, namely the massive unlawful military attacks on our safeguarded nuclear facilities by the U.S. and the Israeli regime.
​
Those aggressions were launched less than 24 hours following the adoption of the US sponsored resolution of this Board in June 2025, and in the midst of negotiations and struck facilities whose material was entirely under safeguards, at a time when Agency inspectors had full presence and access throughout Iran.
​
The Secretariat itself has acknowledged that these attacks created an unprecedented situation, so no one can pretend that this cause is unknown, disputed or irrelevant to the Agency’s  . . .
